coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: 12–14 miles, Z2 only, rolling terrain with 800–1000 ft vert. Your recovery score is 52/100 and your resting HR is 4 bpm above your 30-day average—that's a signal to dial it back. You're 34 days out; this is taper phase and your long run volume is already trending down (31.1 mi this week vs 47.0 last week). Keep this easy, stay aerobic, and use the run to build familiarity with sustained uphill hiking pace without adding fatigue. No tempo, no intervals.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You slept 6.9 hours on a travel schedule—that's below your 30-day average of 8.05h and it matters in taper. Eat a full breakfast before the run (40–50g carbs, protein), and plan to ingest 30–40g carbs/hour during the run if it goes beyond 2.5 hours. Post-run, prioritize protein (25–30g) and carbs within 30 minutes to support recovery. Your body is in a precarious place: moderately fatigued and under-slept. Nutrient timing is non-negotiable this week.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Tonight, target 8+ hours of sleep. You're currently 1.1 hours behind your 30-day average and running a taper—sleep is when adaptation happens. Keep the run easy so you don't add systemic stress. If you're traveling for work today or tomorrow, prioritize a dark hotel room, earplugs, and no alcohol. Cold water immersion or ice baths are off the table during taper; let passive recovery do the work. Your resting HR trending up is a caution flag; sleep will address it faster than any workout.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're in the hardest phase psychologically—the work is done, and doubt creeps in. Today's run is a confidence builder, not a test. The Julian Alps will demand pacing discipline and mental toughness on unforgiving terrain; use these final 34 days to sharpen your hill strategy and practice controlled effort. Your last hard run (12.04 mi @ 132 bpm) was solid. Now prove you can dial it back and still own the uphill. Taper isn't weakness; it's sharpening the knife.
